Subject: MAP kickoff & performance targets for context stress tests

Hannah — thanks again for the demo last week. We want to lock the mutual action plan (MAP) and a concrete benchmark run before legal routes the SOW. High-level asks from our side:

- Validate performance for long-context flows (we have clinical notes up to ~40k tokens).
- Understand TTFT (time-to-first-token) and steady-state throughput at 32k and 40k context lengths.
- Quantify KV cache impact on per-token CPU/GPU cost for repeated prefixes.

Is Redwood able to run a final end-to-end benchmark in our account (dedicated capacity preferred) the week of 30 Nov? We can provide a representative prompt set and synthetic amplification if needed. Also please include a short report we can attach to internal procurement.

Thanks — Ellis
Ellis Burke
Director, Platform Engineering
QuantaMed

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Ellis — thanks, this is clear and aligns with the MAP we discussed. Attached is a draft benchmark plan (quanta_benchmark_plan_v2.pdf) and an evaluation checklist. High-level proposal:

MAP / test scope (short):
- Final run window: 30 Nov - 3 Dec (primary run 3 Dec).
- Test targets: p95 latency <= 220ms (for 1–2k prompt TL; see TTFT target below), sustained throughput 180–250 req/s at concurrency 64–128 depending on seq len, TTFT <= 40ms for cold requests, and TTFT <= 25ms for warm cache.
- Long-context ceilings: functional correctness & perf at 16k, 32k, 40k tokens; measure tail latency and throughput at each step.
- KV cache scenarios: cold/no-cache, warmed-prefix (50% prefix reuse), and KV-only retrieval-heavy flows. We will capture token compute and GPU utilization delta.

Evaluation plan details (attached):
- Test harness: mix of real prompts (you provide) + synthetic expansions to simulate worst-case distribution. Tools: locust for concurrency, a custom tokenizer-aware generator for seq lengths.
- Metrics: TTFT, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, effective throughput (tokens/s and requests/s), GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end service economic estimate ($/1M tokens).
- Pass criteria: p95 latency and TTFT within targets across two consecutive runs and no >10% error-rate increase at max sequence.

Operational asks from QuantaMed:
- Provide 2–3 representative prompt sets (short, medium, long).
- Confirm whether you prefer dedicated capacity on the Redwood Dedicated pool during the run (recommended for determinism).
- Point-of-contact for interference window (who to pause unrelated jobs).

I'll coordinate with Karthik & Marissa on the test harness and the final run. If those targets are acceptable, we'll lock the MAP and sign the SOW.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

On Mon, 23 Nov 2026 at 10:03, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ellis — thanks, this is clear and aligns with the MAP we discussed. Attached is a draft benchmark plan...

Adding implementation notes for the benchmark harness and measurement sanity checks:

- Model variants: we'll run two model families (rwi-7b and rwi-13b-8bit-quant). We'll include a smaller baseline to isolate perf delta.
- Kernel/quantization knobs: test FP16 and int8 paths; capture perf counters for kernel selection.
- Batching policy: measure single-request latency (no batching) and continuous batching (up to 256 tokens or 8ms aggregation window).
- KV cache priming: we will run a warmup pass that writes KV entries for the long-prefixes; then run mixed traffic to measure amortized cost. Priming scripts reference: drive:/warmup/kv_primer.sh (attached in drive link).
- Sequence distributions: use 3 distributions (prod-sampled, uniform-long, spike-long). We'll include a stress synthetic that constructs 40k token prompts by concatenating note fragments — this should expose memory/GC breakpoints.
- Concurrency sweep plan: 1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 256 (stop if error-rate increases >5% or p99 > 2s).

Artifacts we'll produce: CSV exports (kvcache-raw-samples.csv), time-series charts (throughput-20261203.png), and a short write-up with recommendations for caching/fallback strategies.

I'll own the harness and will need QuantaMed's sample prompts and a thumbs-up on the dedicated pool.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final benchmark run results (summary) — 03 Dec 2026

Ellis / team — we completed the controlled benchmark on 03 Dec in your dedicated pool. Summary (high level):

- Configuration: rwi-13b-8bit-quant on a 4x A100 cluster (dedicated), batching: continuous up to 128 tokens, warmup: 5k priming requests to populate KV cache.
- Key results (representative):
  * 1–2k prompts: p95 latency = 190ms, TTFT cold = 38ms, TTFT warm = 22ms, throughput = ~230 req/s.
  * 16k context: p95 latency = 520ms, throughput = ~95 req/s at concurrency 64, p99 spikes to ~1.6s under worst-case prompt composition.
  * 32k context: sustained throughput drops to ~42 req/s at concurrency 32; p95 ~1.2s, p99 > 3s in the spike-long distribution.
  * 40k context: functional correctness maintained for most prompts, but memory pressure caused ~6% additional errors (timeouts); not recommended in production without sharding/fallback.
  * KV cache impact: warmed prefixes reduced token compute by an estimated 34% and improved TTFT by ~12ms on average. Raw samples attached (kvcache-raw-samples.csv).

Observations & recommendations:
- For production latency SLAs at 32k+, we recommend: dedicated shards, request-routing to lower-cost model variants for non-critical requests, and a graceful degradation policy (trim long prefixes after 32k).
- Enable prefix-aware KV caching for frequent patient histories — this was the single largest regression mitigator in our tests.
- For 40k sequences, consider application-level chunking + server-side stitching or a multi-pass retrieval approach to avoid large single-shot requests.

Deliverables: attached charts (throughput-20261203.png), raw CSVs (kvcache-raw-samples.csv), and a one-page procurement summary we'll hand over as a PDF. We'll also prepare the brief SOW addendum for the dedicated window (sow-docusign-qd1187.pdf).

Next steps per MAP:
- You review the artifacts and confirm acceptance.
- Legal/procurement signs the SOW addendum by 01 Dec for the dedicated run (you indicated you had budget; we'll follow DocuSign link).
- If you want, we can schedule a technical readout (30–45m) next week to walk through charts and remediation suggestions.

On a tactical note: we saw the error spike at >32k correlating to a GC sweep on the node; Vivek will follow up with a recommendation for memory tuning and sharding.

— Hannah
Enterprise Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
